notes.meaning: Paul reminds the Christians in Corinth of how he first came to preach to them. He did not use fancy words or human philosophy to impress them. Instead, he simply declared God's own message about Jesus Christ. Our trust should rest on God's truth rather than a speaker's clever style.

Paul made a deliberate choice to focus on Jesus Christ and his death on the cross. He did not let worldly debates or intellectual trends distract him from the core message of salvation. Christ's sacrifice must always remain the center of Christian faith.

When Paul arrived in Corinth, he felt weak, anxious, and deeply humble. He was aware of his own human limits and the real dangers around him, so he put no confidence in his own strength. God often works through our weakness to show his power.

Paul did not try to win people over with smooth speeches or clever human arguments. Instead, his preaching was proven true by the powerful work of the Holy Spirit changing lives. True gospel preaching relies on the Spirit to move people's hearts.

Paul preached simply so that the faith of the believers would rest on God's power rather than human wisdom. If their faith had been built on clever speaking, another speaker could easily talk them out of it. Real faith stands secure because God himself gave it life.

Paul explains that the gospel does contain true wisdom for believers who are spiritually mature. This wisdom is completely different from the ideas of this world and its leaders, whose glory soon fades away. God's wisdom lasts forever, while human power quickly comes to nothing.

Paul speaks of God's wisdom that was once hidden like a secret before Christ was revealed. God planned this path of salvation before time even began so that his people could share in his glory. We can take comfort knowing that God's plan to save us was never an afterthought.

The worldly rulers of that time did not understand God's glorious plan. If they had understood who Jesus really was, they would never have put the Lord of glory to death on a cross. Jesus is called the Lord of glory because he is truly God.

Paul quotes Scripture to show that no human eye, ear, or mind could ever imagine what God has prepared for those who love him. While this includes the joys of heaven, it mainly describes the wonderful spiritual blessings God gives believers right now through the gospel. God provides peace and joy that human senses could never discover on their own.

God has made these hidden truths known to us through his Holy Spirit. The Spirit understands all things completely, even the deepest thoughts and plans of God. Because the Holy Spirit is God, he is able to reveal God's heart to us.

Paul points out that no one knows a person's private thoughts except that person's own spirit inside them. In the same way, no one can know God's inner thoughts except the Spirit of God. We can only know God because his Spirit shares God's truth with us.

Believers have not received the spirit of the world, but the Holy Spirit sent from God. God gave us his Spirit so that we can clearly understand and enjoy all the gifts of grace he has freely given us. Christians can live with peace knowing that God has truly adopted them as his children.

The apostles did not preach using words taught by human philosophy or rhetoric. Instead, they used words taught by the Holy Spirit, matching spiritual truths with spiritual language. We can trust the Scriptures because the Holy Spirit guided the words that were written.

A person without the Holy Spirit cannot accept the truths that come from God. To that person, the gospel sounds like complete foolishness because spiritual truth can only be understood with the Spirit's help. We need God to open our hearts before we can see the value of his truth.

The person who has the Holy Spirit is able to judge and understand spiritual matters rightly. At the same time, worldly people cannot properly judge or understand a believer, because they do not have the Spirit. Walking with God gives believers a clear perspective that the world cannot grasp.

Paul quotes Scripture to ask who could ever know the Lord's mind well enough to give him advice. No mere human can, but believers have the mind of Christ because his Spirit lives within them. When we follow Christ, we begin to see life through his truth and love.
